newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW -Bulmer to forego profits growth.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW -Bulmer to forego profits growth.

text.p: Britain's biggest cider maker H.P. Bulmer Holdings Plc will show no profits growth next year due to a big increase in its advertising budget, said finance director Alan Flockhart on Wednesday.
The company will increase its investment on media advertising to 8.0 million stg from 4.7 million in the year to April 1998. It has also allocated an extra 500,000 stg to new product development.
"This increased investment will absorb the anticipated profits growth for next year," said Flockhart in an interview.
Earlier the company reported a 9.2 percent increase in profits before tax and exceptional items to 30.1 million stg in the year ending April 25, 1997.
Bulmer's decision to spend more on advertising its cider brands, which include Strongbow, Woodpecker and Scrumpy Jack, follows a major re-shape by its main competitor Matthew Clark Plc.

The company's shares plunged 60 percent after a profits warning in September 1996 and in January Matthew Clark was forced to outline a recovery plan aimed at combating the rise in popularity of "alcopops", alcoholic lemonades and sodas, and a severe industry price war.
Part of its plan includes an increase in advertising expenditure to about 8.0 million next year aimed at bringing back 18-to-24 year old drinkers to the cider market.

"The key issue is the fact that the weight of advertising expenditure between the cider market and beer market has been dropping as our major competitors have been using that to prop up their profit line," said Flockhart.
"So we are correcting that imbalance," he added.
"We want to look after our position and make sure that our leadership in brands continues and that involves more investment than we have been making in the last five years," said Flockhart.
The company has faced stiff price competition from its rivals especially on cider sold to supermarkets and the emergence of "alcopops" has enticed many cider drinkers away.
The group also had to contend with an increase in excise duty imposed by government on strong alcohol ciders in October 1996.
In the 12 months to March 1997 cider consumption in Britain at 5.1 million hectare litres declined by 2.7 percent. However over the same period Bulmer showed sales growth of almost three percent.
The company said it now has a 54.5 percent share of Britain's cider market, its highest level for over 30 years.
Bulmer shares were 2-1/2 pence down at 472-1/2 pence by 0900 GMT, while shares in Matthew Clark were 1/2 pence higher at 240-1/2p.
